gaps.note: Founders step back to whisper to each other, largely inaudible.

stage_a.note: F1 smiles broadly and speaks with strong positive engagement about their mission.
F2 shows sustained engaged excitement when describing the problem they are solving.
Friendly initial greeting, but the pitch maintains a serious, purpose-driven tone.

venture.description: Eco-friendly, plastic-free laundry detergent sheets and household cleaning products.
venture.note: The founders state they are seeking $500,000 for 5% of their company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 introduces himself to the panel of investors.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 introduces himself, states the company name, and asks for five hundred thousand dollars for five percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 shares his background flying helicopters in the military and observing global plastic waste, motivating the business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains that the plastic crisis affects cities and oceans, pointing to the laundry industry as a major culprit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they developed a patented, eco-friendly, dehydrated laundry detergent sheet to combat the plastic crisis.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 describes the product as lightweight, mess-free, and one hundred percent plastic-free compared to mainstream liquid detergents.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 concludes the pitch by asking the investors who wants to join their mission to eliminate plastic.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 instructs the investors to roll up the detergent sheet provided to them.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 remarks positively on the scent of the detergent sheet.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 tells the panel to roll the sheet tight enough to fit inside the provided glass bottle.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 instructs them to drop the sheet into the cold water in the bottle, noting it begins to dissolve.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 tells the investors to shake the bottle for a few seconds.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 points out that bubbles have formed in the bottle.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 confirms they have successfully turned the solid sheet into soapy bubbles.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses positive approval of the demonstration.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks about the specific ingredients contained within the detergent sheet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 details the primary plant-based ingredients, noting the absence of synthetic chemicals found in mainstream detergents.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks about the founders' backgrounds, their roles in the company, and how they transitioned from the military.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 details his military career, lung damage from burn pits in Iraq, and his motivation to eliminate plastic waste.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains his fifteen years of entrepreneurial experience and his desire to build a purpose-driven business with F1.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks about the other products displayed on the table besides the laundry sheets.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they have forty-six different SKUs covering various cleaning product categories.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 clarifies that the business sells multiple items rather than just the detergent sheets.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 confirms they sell floor cleaners and scent boosters, though laundry sheets remain the primary focus.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks when the company officially launched its products.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they officially launched to the public in January of twenty twenty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for their total sales figures for the year twenty twenty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 reports just over two million dollars in total sales for twenty twenty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 remarks that the two million dollar sales figure is impressive.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what percentage of their sales comes from their top-selling item.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that the laundry sheets are their best-selling product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for the specific dollar amount of sheet sales out of the two million total.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states sheet sales were 1.2 million and mentions an exclusivity agreement for the patent with Kimberly Clark.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if they pay a royalty to Kimberly Clark for the patent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that they do pay a royalty.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if they are the only company allowed to use the patent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms they have exclusive rights.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if there are any limitations on their exclusive use of the patent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the patent remains exclusive to them as long as they pay their annual royalties.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 points out they do not own the IP and asks how long the agreement with Kimberly Clark lasts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the agreement lasts through October of twenty twenty-four.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks what happens after that date and if they have an option to renew the agreement.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 clarifies that the agreement simply expires.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 exits, citing concerns over the expiring patent, too many SKUs, and her perception that the founders lack salesmanship.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 teases the founders about S4 calling them the worst salesmen she has seen on the show.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters by stating they are on track to reach nearly seven million dollars in sales for the current year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 praises the response and asks for their net profit margin.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states their net profit margin is twenty-four percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks to confirm they are projecting growth from two million to seven million in one year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms the projected growth figure.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks how they achieved such sales growth given S4's criticism of their sales skills.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains they used aggressive advertising campaigns and user-generated content from customers to drive sales.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks which social media platforms they used to run their video advertisements and testimonials.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 lists Pinterest, AdWords, and social platforms, emphasizing his background in marketing and e-commerce rather than traditional sales.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exits, noting a conflict of interest because he is already invested in a competing eco-friendly cleaning company.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 exits, stating that while she likes the mission, the valuation is too high for the equity offered.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks what they specifically plan to do with the five hundred thousand dollar investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains they want to use the funds to expand the business globally and make a worldwide impact.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 exits, disagreeing with the expensive global expansion plan and advising them to conserve their cash instead.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks why they are confident in hitting seven million in sales, noting it would justify their valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 cites over twenty-one thousand monthly subscribers, projecting nearly three million in recurring revenue alone.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 adds they are working with a consumer goods group and hope to enter retail stores soon.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 offers five hundred thousand dollars for ten percent equity, praising their digital marketing skills and subscriber base.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters S5's offer, asking if he would accept eight percent equity, which was their planned ceiling.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 revises his offer to eight percent equity plus two percent in advisory shares to maintain his desired stake.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks to clarify if the revised terms effectively mean ten percent total equity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 confirms the total is ten percent and presses the founders to make a decision on the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks for ten seconds to discuss the offer privately with his co-founder.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 accepts S5's revised offer of eight percent equity and two percent advisory shares.

decisions.note: Concerns over expiring patent, too many SKUs, and lack of salesmanship.
Conflict of interest with his existing portfolio company Blueland.
Valuation is too high for the equity offered.
Disagrees with expensive global expansion plan, advises conserving cash.
Impressed by their digital marketing skills and subscriber base.
Wants to maintain 10% total equity value.
